title: GPU multi-account egress quarantine and Terraform catalog
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This page describes the 'egress quarantine' pattern we use to contain tenants or test workloads that cause unexpected outbound traffic from GPU pools. It pairs prescriptive Terraform modules with CI/CD gating and runbook actions so infra operators can isolate, debug, and remediate noisy egress without broad tenant disruption. The document contains an implementation catalog, sample Terraform/CI snippets, SLOs and alert thresholds, an operator runbook, and a staged rollout checklist.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood GPU tenant VPCs and ephemeral eval sandboxes in cloud accounts managed by eng-infra.
- Focuses on outbound traffic (egress) controls: NAT throughput caps, per-tenant proxying, egress-sidecars, and automated quarantine routing.
- Not in scope: application-level rate limiting inside tenant containers (handled by product teams).

Goals

- Provide a repeatable Terraform module catalog that pairs with CI/CD for safe changes.
- Ensure noisy-tenant egress can be restricted to a quarantined path within 3 minutes of detection.
- Preserve tenant isolation and billing transparency while reducing blast radius of misbehaving workloads.

Ownership

- Primary owners: eng-infra (networking subgroup).
- Pager contact: #infra-oncall (rotation: infra-sre)
- Module maintainers: aisha.patel@redwood.ai, tomas.alvarez@redwood.ai

Architecture overview (text diagram)

- Tenant VPCs -> VPC peering / Transit Gateway -> Central egress VPC -> NAT fleet + Egress Sidecars -> Internet
- Quarantine path: Central egress VPC -> Quarantine-subnet (restricted NAT/IDS) -> Forensics bucket and SIEM forwarder

Key components and responsibilities

- egress-fencing module (Terraform): creates per-tenant NAT Gateways with tokenized rate limits, CloudWatch/Stackdriver metrics, and IAM roles for quota updates. Responsible: networking team.
- tenant-egress-proxy module: deploys an upstream HTTP/TCP proxy cluster (Envoy-based) that supports per-tenant ACLs and request sampling. Responsible: infra-platform.
- quarantine-route module: attaches route table overrides to move traffic from normal NAT to quarantine NAT and applies stricter egress ACLs. Responsible: eng-infra networking.
- egress-sidecar image: lightweight sidecar that collects flow metadata, enforces token buckets on the host, and forwards telemetry to SIEM. Responsible: infra-observability.

Terraform module catalog (summary table)

| Module name | Purpose | Required inputs | Outputs | Recommended version | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| egress-fencing | Per-tenant NAT + rate-limits | tenant_id, cidr, nat_instance_type, egress_bandwidth_limit_mbps | nat_id, nat_public_ip | v1.2.0 | Use v1.2.0+ for metric tags used in alerts |
| tenant-egress-proxy | Envoy ACL cluster, sampling | tenant_id, proxy_instance_size, allowed_destinations | proxy_dns, proxy_security_group | v0.9.3 | Supports ACLs and header enrichment |
| quarantine-route | Route table override to quarantine subnets | tenant_id, quarantine_subnet_id, normal_route_table_id | route_association_id | v0.1.0 | Idempotent; has safety lock flag |
| egress-sidecar | Host-level flow collector & token bucket | image_tag, sampling_rate | sidecar_service_name | v2.0.1 | Includes offline upload to S3 for forensics |

Example Terraform usage (minimal)

```hcl
module "tenant-egress" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@internal.redwood.ai/infra-modules/egress-fencing.git//modules/egress-fencing?ref=v1.2.0"
  tenant_id = "tenant-42"
  cidr = "10.48.0.0/20"
  nat_instance_type = "t3.medium"
  egress_bandwidth_limit_mbps = 250
}

module "tenant-proxy" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@internal.redwood.ai/infra-modules/tenant-egress-proxy.git?ref=v0.9.3"
  tenant_id = "tenant-42"
  proxy_instance_size = "c5.large"
  allowed_destinations = ["api.redwood.ai", "datasets.example.com:443"]
}
```

CI/CD and gating recommendations

- All changes to the modules live in the infra-modules monorepo and must pass the following pipelines: terraform fmt -> unit tests (terratest) -> plan approval -> canary apply (sandbox only) -> staged apply to prod using promote job.
- Buildkite job sample (condensed):

```yaml
steps:
  - label: ":terraform: fmt & validate"
    command: ["./ci/run-fmt-and-validate.sh"]
  - label: ":test_tube: terratest"
    command: ["./ci/run-terratest.sh"]
    parallelism: 4
  - wait: ~
  - label: ":eyes: plan"
    command: ["./ci/plan.sh"]
    env:
      TF_VAR_target_workspace: "canary"
  - label: ":shipit: apply canary"
    command: ["./ci/apply.sh canary"]
    if: "branch = main AND build.state = passed"
```

Safety controls enforced by CI:

1) plan diffs that widen egress CIDRs or remove quarantine-route module must be blocked and require manual approval.
2) Any increase in nat_instance_type size that impacts shared billing tiers triggers an owners-review label.
3) Module releases require changelog, migration plan, and at least two reviewers.

Monitoring, alerts and SLOs

- Primary metrics: outbound_bytes_per_minute_per_tenant, nat_connections_open, proxy_5xx_rate, quarantine_rate (percentage of tenants currently in quarantine).
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - P1: outbound_bytes_per_minute_per_tenant > 5000 MB for 5m -> page infra-oncall. Objective: detect runaway dataset exfil.
  - P2: nat_connections_open > 100k for 5m -> page infra-oncall and network owner. Objective: detect amplification attacks.
  - P3: proxy_5xx_rate > 5% for 3m after deploy -> page platform-oncall. Objective: detect proxy misconfiguration.
- SLOs: Quarantine activation time <= 3 minutes from alerting window (target 99th percentile).

Operator runbook: noisy egress detected

1) Triage alert in PagerDuty -> join #infra-egress channel. Gather initial facts: tenant_id, metric window, top-destinations (via FlowLogs query), current route table associations.
2) If outbound_bytes_per_minute_per_tenant > 1000 MB and destination set is large (>10 unique /24s), immediately execute quarantine route change (see commands below).
3) Run the forensics collection script to snapshot flow logs and sample pcap for 5 minutes. Upload artifacts to s3://redwood-forensics/tenant-<id>/YYYYMMDD-HHMM.
4) Notify customer success (if customer-managed tenant) and apply billing tag 'egress-quarantine:<incident-id>' for chargeback visibility.
5) Work with product/security to decide: throttle (reduce nat instance credit), quarantine (route override), or unblock (if false positive).

CLI quick actions (ops)

- To attach quarantine route (Terraformless quick action):

```bash
# This wrapper calls AWS CLI and our internal route-association helper
scripts/ops/quarantine-route.sh --tenant tenant-42 --quarantine-subnet subnet-0a1b2c --reason "noisy-egress-20250114-1"
```

- To revert quarantine:

```bash
scripts/ops/revert-quarantine.sh --tenant tenant-42 --incident incident-20250114-1
```

- To collect flow logs (5 minute sample):

```bash
scripts/ops/collect-flowlogs.sh --tenant tenant-42 --window 5m --out s3://redwood-forensics/tenant-42/$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M)
```

Post-incident analysis and postmortem requirements

- For any P1, the oncall must open a postmortem within 72 hours and link the incident to the related_pages above. Include: timeline, root cause, mitigations, and a migration or preventive task ticket.
- For quarantines that lasted > 1 hour, mandatory action: implement service-level limits or ACLs in tenant-egress-proxy and schedule a follow-up test run.

Rollout plan for the catalog modules

1) Canary: release to a set of 10 sandbox tenants for 2 weeks. Observe proxy_5xx_rate and outbound_bytes metrics.
2) Stage: release to dev and staging accounts (50 tenants) for 1 week. Run chaos tests that simulate 2x egress.
3) Gradual prod rollout: ramp to 25% GPU production tenants per day with automatic rollback gate on P2 alerts.
4) Full rollout: require cross-team sign-off and update of runbook with any new commands.

Testing checklist before apply to production

- [ ] terratest coverage for new module paths > 80%
- [ ] Integration test that flips quarantine-route and verifies telemetry in SIEM
- [ ] Performance test: NAT throughput at expected limits with sidecar enabled
- [ ] Access review of new IAM roles created by modules

Security and compliance considerations

- Quarantine flows and copied artifacts stored in forensics bucket are encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys when tenant is enterprise-grade.
- Audit logs of route-association changes are shipped to the central audit index for 1 year by default.
- Any change to quarantine behavior must be reviewed by security for data-exfil risk if the tenant stores regulated data.

Appendix: small checklist of terraform commands and safety flags

- Create a feature branch, run lint and unit tests: `git checkout -b feature/egress-fencing` && `make test`
- Plan against canary workspace: `TF_WORKSPACE=canary make plan MODULE=egress-fencing`
- Apply with safety lock (prevents route changes without manual approval): `TF_FORCE_LOCK=yes make apply MODULE=egress-fencing WORKSPACE=production`

Related docs and references

- See module API reference in infra-modules monorepo: git@internal.redwood.ai:infra-modules/egress-fencing (README + examples).
- Forensics retention policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/egress-forensics-retention.json
- Network telemetry dashboard: /dashboards/network/egress-overview
